No goal was found without a corresponding criterion.

Acceptance criteria describe externally observable outcomes throughout: schema-validation results (AC-008, AC-009, AC-017), exit codes (AC-013), byte-identical file comparisons (AC-016, AC-022, AC-023), diagnostic-line string format (AC-014), and grep-based self-checks (AC-025, AC-034, AC-059). The calibration's element 4 requires 'a commit reference or a SHA-256 fingerprint for that artifact, never a bare path alone' for exactly this artifact category, and its own disqualification rule states that when any element is 'given only as a bare path with no commit or sha256, ... the declaration does not apply: judge phase-sequencing exactly as the default Phase-1 calibration above requires, with no benefit of the doubt.' Downstream failure mode: without a conforming declaration, a task author or quality-gate verifier has no legible mechanism distinguishing this package's dense, structural dependence on design.md/tasks.md content (e.g. REQ-001's Processing clause citing 'design.md's API / Contract Plan' at requirements.md:250-258; AC-026/AC-027/AC-042/AC-046/AC-053 citing tasks.md's 'Deferred, not scheduled' status) from an unauthorized phase-skip, because the one mechanism that would legibly authorize it fails its own evidence bar. Severity is Critical per the calibration's own Severity Calibration text: absent a valid declaration, citing later-phase artifacts from a Pending spec package is 'an unsafe or unauthorized workflow boundary ... that makes the specification unreviewable.'
